baseline.working_tree: Current shared checkout; new frozen brand/writing rules are uncommitted additions. Component files and example sources are individually hashed below.

scope: Static, full-text review of every component guide and its referenced example source against the 33 frozen brand rules and 68 frozen writing rules. The chart harness was read because it generates the chart example content. No existing component or example was edited.
limits: This is not a browser, assistive-technology, usability, live Home Assistant or device-control audit.
No confirmed finding means no concrete static-content contradiction was identified in the stated scope; it is not full compliance or an accessibility pass.
Shared stylesheet drift is owned by the parent foundation audit and is not duplicated here.
Older original SVG metadata is recorded as a migration recommendation because BG-ILL-10 governs new asset delivery. Functional icon and map strokes are not expressive-illustration violations.

findings.title: Give fixed reading and maintenance examples an unambiguous date and time context

evidence.excerpt:
"html": "

Living room temperature

20 \u00b0C \u2014 example reading. Updated at 14:30.

",
evidence.reason: The fixed example has a clock time but no date, zone or distinction between observation and display update.

evidence.excerpt: Electricity imported today:3.8 kWh
evidence.reason: The fixed daily energy total uses an unanchored today, so the period cannot be identified outside the authoring day.

evidence.excerpt: Energy history may be delayed tonight.
evidence.reason: The maintenance notice uses tonight without a date.

evidence.excerpt: The example recording service is scheduled for maintenance from 02:00 to 02:30. Device controls are not part of this example notice.
evidence.reason: The maintenance window has no date or timezone.

evidence.excerpt: <caption class="govuk-table__caption govuk-table__caption--m">Room temperatures</caption>
evidence.reason: The room-temperature table has no observation date/time.

evidence.excerpt: <caption class="govuk-table__caption govuk-table__caption--m">Electricity recorded by hour</caption>
evidence.reason: Hourly rows identify clock times and GMT but not their calendar date.

evidence.excerpt: <caption class="govuk-table__caption govuk-table__caption--m">Room temperatures at 09:00 GMT</caption>
evidence.reason: The comparison identifies clock time and weekdays but no week/date range.

findings.why_it_matters: These reusable examples teach context for operational readings and schedules. Their synthetic-data status prevents a live-data claim, but does not identify the period or time represented. A copied or standalone specimen remains ambiguous.
findings.proposed_change: Add explicit invented observation dates or selected-period captions, and the relevant zone. Label observed/reported/period-start accurately. Give the maintenance notice one full dated window; give the weekday comparison calendar dates or a week commencing date. Keep all data synthetic and unchanged.
acceptance: Each standalone example identifies the relevant date/period and timezone without depending on the real current day.
Displayed clock values and time datetime attributes agree, and observation/interval labels match the example model.
The examples still explicitly remain invented and do not claim a live outage or reading.

findings.title: Make the sample-day control and caption agree with the displayed chart

evidence.excerpt: const nextDay = element('button', 'Show next sample day'); nextDay.type = 'button';
evidence.reason: The advertised action is created for every isolated example.

evidence.excerpt: for (const key of ['power', 'usage', 'many'] as Key[]) {
evidence.reason: The handler excludes devices and empty, although their isolated examples still show the action.

evidence.excerpt: cards[key].shadowRoot!.querySelector('.chart-description')!.textContent = `Invented example values for ${11 + day} November 2026. See the table for the original times, period starts and units.`;
evidence.reason: The caption constructs a November day number independently of the real timestamp and becomes invalid after 30 November.

findings.why_it_matters: An isolated device or no-data example advertises a day change that it does not perform. For the supported examples, repeated clicks eventually show a nonexistent date while the source timestamp has moved into December. This is confined to the documentation harness; it is not a finding against the production adapter.
findings.proposed_change: Either implement selected-period changes for every advertised chart or only show the control where it has a defined effect. Format captions from the same actual sample timestamp used for data and axes, including month/year boundaries and comparison context. Keep the production adapter and data semantics unchanged.
acceptance: For each isolated example, the control has a truthful visible effect or is omitted with an explained limit.
Advancing from 30 November to 1 December produces a valid caption matching plotted and tabular dates.
Current/comparison periods remain correctly labelled after repeated day changes and theme changes.

findings.title: Describe the second action-link example as the destination it actually provides

evidence.excerpt: The [NHS action link](https://service-manual.nhs.uk/design-system/components/action-link) emphasises entry to a service journey. civica.uk also uses this treatment for a small number of frequently used dashboard destinations. That is a deliberate local extension: a link still navigates and never sends a device command. The examples distinguish a task entry from a help destination.
evidence.reason: The guide says the pair distinguishes a task entry from a help destination.

evidence.excerpt: Review display preferences
evidence.reason: The second example is a display-preference task with an in-frame settings section, not a help destination.

findings.why_it_matters: The guide and its example describe different purposes. Both existing destinations are safe local links; the issue is instructional accuracy, not routing safety.
findings.proposed_change: Either make the second specimen a clearly labelled help destination with useful help content, or change the guide to describe the actual task-entry and display-preference examples. Keep link purpose and accessible name aligned.
acceptance: The guide, example title/description, visible link and target section describe the same destination type.
The link still uses a real existing local target and sends no device command.

findings.title: Restore spaces after punctuation in component guidance and examples

evidence.excerpt: Test long names,320px width, increased text size and direct navigation into a child page. Ensure the current page heading and parent trail agree.
evidence.reason: The comma runs directly into the following width.

evidence.excerpt: Test missing parts,31 February, an unexpected future date and mobile number keyboards. Explain any domain-specific date restriction in plain language rather than rejecting it as “invalid”.
evidence.reason: The comma runs into the date example.

evidence.excerpt: Example limit:40 characters
evidence.reason: The colon runs into the limit.

evidence.excerpt: Electricity imported today:3.8 kWh
evidence.reason: The colon runs into the displayed value.

evidence.excerpt: Last reported change:11 November 2026 at 14:00 GMT.
evidence.reason: The colon runs into the date.

findings.why_it_matters: These are authored prose separators, not literal entity IDs, times, paths or user names. The missing spaces make instructional copy harder to scan and are inconsistent with the adopted punctuation default.
findings.proposed_change: Insert a normal space after each listed comma or label colon. Preserve numeric clock syntax, paths, identifiers and supplied names. Resolve the daily-total date context under AUD-COMP-001 at the same time.
acceptance: The cited strings use conventional prose spacing without changing literal values.
Example source and rendered copy stay in sync.

recommendations.recommendation: When these existing specimens are next changed, record creator/provenance, rights, intended background, purpose and alternative-text decision in their records, as done for the new brand examples. Preserve their functional strokes and schematic map boundaries.
recommendations.not_a_confirmed_violation: BG-ILL-10 explicitly covers new asset delivery; these assets predate the frozen rule set. Functional icons and spatial diagrams are not subject to the expressive illustration no-outline rule.

evidence.excerpt:
"html": "

Kitchen light

Waiting for the device to respond

Keep the last confirmed state visible until a new state arrives. This static example does not complete automatically.

",
evidence.reason: The specimen states the implementation principle but does not show a concrete last reported state or timestamp.

recommendations.recommendation: Add an invented last reported state and its time alongside the pending request so authors can see the complete pattern. Keep the message explicit that the static example does not complete automatically.
recommendations.not_a_confirmed_violation: The specimen correctly labels a pending state and does not claim a confirmed result. This would improve coverage rather than establish a current unsafe behaviour.

evidence.excerpt: title: "Keep text when a save fails validation"
evidence.reason: The title promises an example of retaining entered text.

evidence.excerpt: <textarea class="govuk-textarea govuk-textarea--error" id="required-description" name="required-description" rows="4" aria-describedby="required-description-hint required-description-error" aria-invalid="true" >
evidence.reason: The textarea contains no substantive entered answer, so it demonstrates a required-field error rather than retention.

recommendations.recommendation: Either relabel this as a missing-required-description example, or show a non-empty description preserved while a different field fails validation. Do not invent an arbitrary length restriction merely to make its text invalid.
recommendations.not_a_confirmed_violation: An empty answer can accurately fail required validation; no input is visibly discarded. The current example is weak evidence for retention, not proof of a retention bug.
